patterns.title: Rain falls more on weekends than weekdays
patterns.headline: The dataset has one value per month, so it cannot say which weekday rain fell on. Nothing is shown for this claim because no data backs it.
patterns.method: Needs daily rainfall. Run scripts/test_weekend_rain.py (Open-Meteo daily archive, 2005–2024) with internet access; it reports mean rain on wet days by weekday with a Kruskal–Wallis test.
patterns.caveat: Even with daily data, 20 years in one city is a small sample and weekday effects are usually weak, so expect a null result.

patterns.title: Smog is worse during the crop-burning season
patterns.headline: In Punjab, PM2.5 averages 86.4 µg/m³ in Oct–Nov (rice-stubble burning season) vs 60.8 the rest of the year, 1.42× higher. Cities outside Punjab show no such jump.
patterns.method: Mann–Whitney test of Oct–Nov vs other months, 20 years of monthly PM2.5 per city group.
patterns.caveat: This is a seasonal coincidence, not proof of burning. Oct–Nov in Punjab is also very dry (7.9 mm vs 44 mm yearly average) and has cold, stagnant air. The dataset has no fire counts; NASA FIRMS (in your dataset plan) is needed to link smog to actual burning.

patterns.title: Rain cleans the air in Punjab and Hyderabad
patterns.unit: µg/m³ PM2.5 vs the city's normal for that month
patterns.headline: After removing the normal seasonal cycle, months drier than usual have higher-than-normal PM2.5 and wetter months lower, in 4 of 8 cities (strongest in Multan, ρ = -0.39).
patterns.method: Seasonal anomalies (value minus that city's average for the calendar month); Spearman correlation of PM2.5 vs rainfall anomalies, plus the driest vs wettest quarter of months.
patterns.caveat: Correlation, not proof of wash-out. Dry spells also coincide with stagnant weather. Islamabad, Peshawar and Quetta show no significant effect.

patterns.title: Nitrogen dioxide builds up in winter
patterns.headline: NO₂ is higher in Dec–Feb than Jun–Aug in 7 of 8 cities, up to 2.81× in Karachi. Quetta is the exception.
patterns.method: Mann–Whitney test of winter vs summer monthly NO₂ columns, 2005–2024.
patterns.caveat: Winter inversions trap pollution and NO₂ lasts longer in cold weather, so the satellite column rises even with unchanged emissions. It is not purely a measure of more traffic or industry.

patterns.title: June–July is the haziest stretch of the year
patterns.headline: Aerosol load is 1.43–1.73× higher in Jun–Jul than the rest of the year, in all 8 cities, including dry Quetta and Karachi.
patterns.method: Mann–Whitney test of Jun–Jul AOD vs other months.
patterns.caveat: Consistent with pre-monsoon dust and humid-air haze, but AOD alone cannot tell dust from smoke or moisture-swollen particles.
